How to read this table. Each row is one city or dealer zone; each number is its revenue in ₹ Cr a month at the end of that quarter, and darker cells earn more. Click a name to split it by product line; click any number to see on the right how it is built. Use City / Dealer / Both to filter, and “Show unopened units” to add the cities and zones not yet opened.
Why it matters. No revenue in the forecast appears without a named city or dealer zone behind it, so each number can be checked unit by unit.
Revenue by planning unit. City and dealer-zone sales contribute to product revenue. Future locations are planning allocations; only the four live locations are named.

How to read this page. Each card is one product line’s revenue, in ₹ Cr a month, from Q1 to Q16, across all cities and dealer zones. Every card uses the same scale, so heights compare directly. The two bars under each chart show reach: of the cities, and dealer zones, open at the chosen quarter, how many already sell this line. Change the quarter with “Coverage at”.
Why it matters. Lines beyond tile adhesive bring ${Math.round((1-view(SCOPE.core).M.tile[15]/view(SCOPE.core).T[15])*100)}% of Q16 revenue; this page shows when each one starts and how far it has reached.
Revenue by product. Launch timing and channel coverage explain the sales mix. All charts use the same scale. Coverage counts locations selling each product.

All chart and split values are ₹ Cr/month. Display amounts are rounded; CSV exports retain full precision. Equivalent MoM is inferred as (current-quarter MRR ÷ previous-quarter MRR)^(1/3) − 1. Annual ARR at Q16 = Q16 MRR × 12. Revenue values are quarter-end monthly run rates. Cash estimates interpolate the intervening months separately.
Revenue basis. ₹ Cr/month at quarter end. ARR = monthly revenue × 12. Cash calculations estimate the intervening months separately.

These are numbered planning allocations, not named-city forecasts. Rounded row values can sum differently from rounded totals; portfolio totals always read the existing forecast directly. A dash means zero.
Future locations. Numbered planning units for the expansion forecast. Figures are rounded; a dash means zero.

These totals are the model of record shared in the revenue chain. The unit mechanics on this page reproduce them within ${fd(allocationAudit().tie*100,2)}% in every product and quarter; each unit row is scaled by that small factor so units add up exactly.
Product revenue targets. Unit allocations are adjusted to match the fixed targets.

Cost assumptions: ₹${fd(low,1)} L/month budget floor below ₹${fd(A[0]/100,1)} Cr MRR; line-by-line interpolation between supplied anchors; above ₹${fd(A.at(-1)/100,1)} Cr, each line continues at its marginal growth from ₹${fd(A[ref]/100,1)} Cr to ₹${fd(A.at(-1)/100,1)} Cr (₹${fd(marginal,2)} of additional overhead per ₹100 additional revenue). Waterproofing copies wood’s RT/DD costs. Blank discounts are zero. Component calculations retain the 0.5 percentage points rounded in the supplied CM2 display.

Common overhead. Monthly costs linked to revenue levels. Assumption: ₹${fd(low,0)} lakh/month floor. Above ₹${fd(A.at(-1)/100,0)} Cr monthly revenue, costs extend the supplied ₹${fd(A[ref]/100,0)}–${fd(A.at(-1)/100,0)} Cr trend.

Debt proceeds are financing, not earnings. Plant principal is repaid after the grace period; the WC facility follows the selected share of additional working capital.
Debt funding. Borrowing reduces the equity required and adds repayment costs.

Debt coverage applies to additional working capital and/or the three factories. Experience centres, labs, systems and misc are excluded from plant borrowing. Rates are illustrative; interest uses average quarterly debt balances.
Debt eligibility. Added working capital and the three factories. Other investment stays equity-funded.

NOTES[NOTE_WC-1]='Working-capital policy: target = days / 365 × annualised revenue (12 × quarter-end monthly revenue). At 60 days this is 16.44% of ARR.
